name: Talleyrand Martin
role: Medora druggist, weather observer and Billings County coroner
bio: Talleyrand Martin ran the Medora drug store with Dr. Jorgens from late 1884 and kept the town's weather record, which the Cow Boy printed regularly from December 1884. In April 1885 he was collecting Bad Lands petrified specimens, and the drug store moved into what the paper called the best store room in town. In May 1885 the paper began running his report weekly, and he sent six months of observations to Gen. W. B. Hazen, chief of the weather bureau, who added him to its volunteer contributors. He was elected Billings County coroner in April 1886, served as a judge at the election organizing Medora's school township, and in September 1886 published a detailed report on a July heat the paper called remarkable. He was again on the ticket for coroner and among the successful candidates in November 1886.
